title: Frontier AI Safety and Alignment Research Scientist, DeepMind
location: Mountain View, CA, USA ; New York, NY, USA
desc: As an organization, Google maintains a portfolio of research projects driven by fundamental research, new product innovation, product contribution and infrastructure goals, while providing individuals and teams the freedom to emphasize specific types of work. As a Research Scientist, you'll setup large-scale tests and deploy promising ideas quickly and broadly, managing deadlines and deliverables while applying the latest theories to develop new and improved products, processes, or technologies. From creating experiments and prototyping implementations to designing new architectures, our research scientists work on real-world problems that span the breadth of computer science, such as machine (and deep) learning, data mining, natural language processing, hardware and software performance analysis, improving compilers for mobile platforms, as well as core search and much more. As a Research Scientist, you'll also actively contribute to the wider research community by sharing and publishing your findings, with ideas inspired by internal projects as well as from collaborations with research programs at partner universities and technical institutes all over the world. Artificial intelligence will be one of humanity’s most transformative inventions. At Google DeepMind, we are a pioneering AI lab with exceptional interdisciplinary teams focused on advancing AI development to solve complex global challenges and accelerate high-quality product innovation for billions of users. We use our technologies for widespread public benefit and scientific discovery, ensuring safety and ethics are always our highest priority. We are pushing the boundaries across multiple domains. Our global teams offer diverse learning opportunities and varied career pathways for those driven to achieve exceptional results through collective effort. Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. US: $174000 - $252000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits Learn more about benefits at Google . Lead foundational and empirical research in AI safety and alignment, from mathematical formulation and algorithmic design through validation on frontier architectures. Characterize failure modes in frontier models, including newly uncovered ones, using interpretability research (mechanistic, latent-space, or black-box), and turn those findings into safeguards, mitigations, and alignment improvements. Propose novel research directions and develop scalable alignment and control interventions, including reinforcement learning methods, that anticipate vulnerabilities as AI systems become increasingly complex. Share research outcomes with internal teams across DeepMind and publish them at premier peer-reviewed AI conferences and venues. Collaborate with frontier modeling, safety, security, and product teams across DeepMind to turn scientific breakthroughs into deployed safeguards. Minimum qualifications: Master's degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Applied Mathematics, a related quantitative technical field, or equivalent practical experience. 3 years of experience in large language models (LLM) or diffusion models: including interpretability, reinforcement learning (RL), pre-training, or representation engineering, or architectural design. Published paper(s) in machine learning or theoretical computer science conferences (e.g., NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, AISTATS, COLT, ALT, STOC, FOCS, SODA Deep learning experience evidenced by scientific papers or GitHub repositories (e.g., neural network architectures, representation space discoveries, quantization, or sparsity). Industry experience working with AI-assisted coding and AI tools. Preferred qualifications: 2 years of experience in AI safety, responsibility, security, or red-teaming. 1 year of experience developing multi-agent frameworks or autonomous agent systems. 1 year of experience researching alignment or mitigation in the latent space (e.g., mechanistic interpretability, activation steering, latent monitoring). Experience training, post-training, or evaluating large-scale foundation models using JAX, PyTorch, or TensorFlow. Experience leading multi-researcher projects from mathematical formulation to empirical validation across research and product teams. Master's degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Applied Mathematics, a related quantitative technical field, or equivalent practical experience. 3 years of experience in large language models (LLM) or diffusion models: including interpretability, reinforcement learning (RL), pre-training, or representation engineering, or architectural design. Industry experience working with AI-assisted coding and AI tools.

title: Quant Research Analyst
location: Newport Beach, CA USA ; Newport Beach, CA USA (United States of America)
desc: PIMCO is a global leader in active fixed income with deep expertise across public and private markets. We invest our clients’ capital across a range of fixed income and credit opportunities, leveraging our decades of experience navigating complex debt markets. Our flexible capital base and deep relationships with issuers have helped us become one of the world’s largest providers of traditional and nontraditional solutions for companies that need financing and investors who seek strong risk-adjusted returns. Since 1971, our people have shaped our organization through a high-performance inclusive culture, in which we celebrate diverse thinking. We invest in our people and strive to imprint our CORE values of Collaboration, Openness, Responsibility and Excellence. We believe each of us is here to help others succeed and this has led to PIMCO being recognized as an innovator, industry thought leader and trusted advisor to our clients. Role Overview We are seeking a Surveillance Data Scientist to help build and scale surveillance capabilities across private asset-backed finance. Sitting at the intersection of investments, data and technology, the role will develop analytical tools and data infrastructure that enable Portfolio Managers, Asset Management and Risk to monitor performance, compare realized outcomes with underwriting assumptions and identify emerging risks and opportunities. Responsibilities Design and build analytical tools for private asset-backed investments, including loan-level performance aggregators, return calculators, benchmarking tools and exception identification. Build and automate data flows with Technology to support accurate exposure, collateral, cash-flow and performance monitoring. Develop consistent surveillance across standardized asset types such as consumer loans, student loans and auto finance, and extend capabilities over time to mortgage whole loans and other private asset classes. Reconcile realized performance against underwriting assumptions, identify material variances and help translate findings into actionable insights for Portfolio Managers, Asset Management and Risk. Partner with public- and private-side Technology teams to develop reusable tools and APIs for investment and analytical platforms. Work directly with Portfolio Managers, Asset Management, Risk and quantitative modelers to identify gaps in investment performance analysis, assumptions and models. Produce clear surveillance reporting and, over time, targeted sector research to identify performance trends and relative-value opportunities. Requirements Master's degree in Financial Engineering, quantitative finance, statistics, applied mathematics, computer science or a related quantitative discipline. Strong quantitative skills and a solid understanding of structured credit and asset-backed investments; experience with private credit or asset-backed finance is strongly preferred. Hands-on working knowledge of Python and SQL, with the ability to query data, develop analytical tools and automate repeatable processes. Experience working with loan-level, collateral, cash-flow or investment-performance data and translating analysis into practical investment insights. Ability to work independently in an evolving environment, shape solutions from ambiguous requirements and partner effectively across investment, risk and technology teams. Strong written and verbal communication. PIMCO follows a total compensation approach when rewarding employees which includes a base salary and a discretionary bonus. Base salary is the fixed component of compensation that is determined by core job responsibilities, relevant experience, internal level, and market factors. The discretionary bonus is used to award performance and therefore is determined by company, business, team, and individual performance. Salary Range: $ 205,000.00 - $ 240,000.00 Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action Statement PIMCO recruits and hires qualified candidates without regard to race, national origin, ancestry, religion (including religious dress and grooming practices), sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender (including gender identity and expression), age, military or veteran status, disability (physical or mental), any factor prohibited by law, and as such affirms in policy and practice to support and promote the concept of equal employment opportunity and affirmative action, in accordance with all applicable federal, state, provincial and municipal laws. The company also prohibits discrimination on other basis such as medical condition, or marital status under applicable laws. Applicants with Disabilities PIMCO
